band.changedElsewhere: Changed by someone else: read the page again to see it.

rounding.title: Rounding, tolerance and grace
rounding.purpose: How clock events become hours. It counts from each day's next computation; an approved day keeps its figures.
rounding.early: Early clock-in counts from shift start
rounding.earlyHint: Clocking in before the shift adds no time.
rounding.fixedBreaksHint: Off: people clock out for a break.
rounding.autoHint: After the shift ends, plus this tolerance. The day is flagged for a person to look at.

problem.lateGraceMinutes: Give the grace as 0 to 60 minutes.
problem.overtimeUnitMinutes: Count overtime in units of 1 to 60 minutes.
problem.autoClockOutAfterMinutes: Close it 0 to 720 minutes after the shift ends.

example.earlyOn: A clock-in at 05:52 for a 06:00 shift counts from 06:00.
example.earlyOff: A clock-in at 05:52 for a 06:00 shift counts from {time}: the minutes before 06:00 count only as overtime.
example.graceOn: A clock-in up to {until} still counts from 06:00; at {after} it counts from {counted}.
example.graceNone: A clock-in after 06:00 counts from that minute (no lateness grace).
example.graceNoneRounded: A clock-in after 06:00 counts from that minute, rounded (no lateness grace).
example.roundOn: Clock events are rounded to the nearest {unit} minutes: 13:52 counts as {a}, 13:53 as {b}.
example.roundOff: Clock events are not rounded: they count to the minute.
example.overtime: Overtime counts in whole units of {unit} minutes: a clock-out {after} minutes after a 14:00 shift end gives {unit} minutes.
example.overtimeLong: Overtime counts in whole units of {unit} minutes: a clock-out {after} minutes after a 14:00 shift end gives {unit} minutes; {less} minutes after it gives none.
example.autoNever: An open clock-in is never closed automatically: the day is flagged for a person to fix.
example.autoAfter: An open clock-in is closed automatically {minutes} minutes after the shift ends, and the day is flagged for a person to look at.
example.breaksFixed: Breaks come from the shift and are deducted automatically; nobody clocks them.
example.breaksClocked: People clock out for a break and back in; the clocked breaks are deducted.

code.title: Absence codes
code.purpose: Codes for the LUL and payroll. An archived code stays readable on its days.
code.codeHint: 1 to 8 capital letters and digits, starting with a letter.
code.lulHint: From the labour consultant; empty until they give it.
code.documentHint: Only a number, such as a certificate's protocol.
code.reachHint: Needs a role over every company.
code.foot: The standard list holds the usual Italian codes to review: their LUL codes come from the labour consultant.
code.sensitive: For this category Nexus keeps a certificate's number at most, never a diagnosis.
code.lawPlain: Health and family data are special categories of personal data.

problem.code: 1 to 8 capital letters and digits, starting with a letter.
problem.labelI18n: Give the name in Italian at least.
problem.lulCode: 1 to 16 letters, digits, dots, hyphens or underscores.

limits.title: Working-time limits
limits.purpose: Warnings before the law is broken.
limits.waitingScope: Save or discard this card to see the site chosen in the top bar.
limits.useLaw: Use the wider limit or the law

problem.limitMinutes: Looser than the law: it needs the CCNL article that allows it.
problem.breakMinutes: The law asks at least 10 minutes: less needs the CCNL article.
problem.referenceMonths: The law says 4 months: longer needs the CCNL article.
problem.alertRoles: Check who is alerted (8 roles at most).

privacy.title: Privacy of people data
privacy.purpose: Who sees individual figures and how small a group may be shown.
privacy.groupHint: A smaller group never shows its figures. {min} is the lowest.
privacy.roles: Roles that see one person's figures, besides the worker
privacy.rolesHint: A role here must also hold the right to open figures; every opening is recorded.
privacy.widenHint: This widens who sees people's figures: it needs a reason and a fresh code.

problem.size: The group size goes from 3 to 50.

item.basis: The site's legal basis is recorded

law.noticePlain: Workers are told how their data is used, before it is used.
law.dpiaPlain: A risk to people's rights is assessed first.
law.ATTENDANCEPlain: A tool that records work needs no agreement, but the workers must be told.
law.PERFORMANCEPlain: A tool that can monitor work needs an agreement or an authorisation.

gate.who: Who sees one person's figures at this site
gate.whoLead: The worker, the team lead and HR
gate.whoLeadHint: The recorded basis covers leads. Widening needs a fresh code.
gate.whoLeadHeld: Held: the recorded basis does not cover leads.
gate.leadsBody: Team leads will see one person's figures of their own team. Each opening is recorded.

onBody.ATTENDANCE: Clock-in and attendance days start at this site. The worker notice and the impact assessment in force are recorded with this decision.
onBody.PERFORMANCE: One person's work figures open at this site, for the worker and HR, one person at a time. The site's basis, the notice and the assessment are recorded with this decision.

offBody.ATTENDANCE: Attendance closes at this site: per-person reads are refused from now on. What was recorded stays. Switching on again is a new decision.
offBody.PERFORMANCE: One person's figures close at this site. Switching on again is a new decision.

gate.basisReferenceHint: The opinion's author and date, or the agreement's number and date.
gate.siteBasis: Basis of this site: {basis}. To change it, use Production › Settings.
gate.coversHint: Only an agreement or an authorisation can say so.
gate.leads: Leads see figures from the start

problem.basis: Give the basis and its reference first.

note.dpiaReview: The impact assessment (version {version}) was due for review on {day}: review it.
note.stationOnly: This site's floor records name the station only: no work figure about one person is recorded here.
note.noticeChanged: The worker notice changed since this was switched on: switch off and on again to record the one in force.
note.dpiaChanged: The impact assessment changed since this was switched on: check it still covers this, then switch off and on again.
note.basisChanged: The site's legal basis changed since this was switched on: switch off and on again to record the one in force.
note.other: Something changed since this was switched on: check it.

stepUp.title: Your code
stepUp.widen: Widening who sees people's figures needs a fresh code from your authenticator app.
stepUp.leads: Letting leads see figures needs a fresh code from your authenticator app.
stepUp.switchOn: Switching this on needs a fresh code from your authenticator app.

problem.locked: Too many tries: wait a moment.
problem.unavailable: The code could not be checked: try again.

done.rounding: Rounding rules saved: they count from each day's next computation.
done.standard_one: {count} code added from the standard list.
done.standard_other: {count} codes added from the standard list.
done.widened: Team leads see figures at this site.
done.narrowed: Team leads no longer see figures at this site.

held.noAudit: Your role does not read the audit log.
held.noAttendance: Your role reads these rules and does not change them.
held.noLimits: Your role reads these limits and does not change them.

field.codeTaken: This code exists already: codes are unique across the group.
field.legalReference: Name the law or the CCNL article.
field.reason: Say why, in a few words.
field.basis: Check the basis and its reference.
field.basisCoversLeads: The basis recorded does not cover leads.
field.leadsSeeFigures: Leads see figures only where the recorded basis covers them.
field.minimumGroupSize: The group size goes from 3 to 50.

leave.title: Unsaved changes
leave.body: You changed these settings and did not save them.
